items.description: "Automated backups for RGW/S3 buckets and Ceph-backed data — today redundancy exists but no copy-off-cluster." — narrowed by ruling T2 to RGW/S3 buckets and by ruling T3 to prd-stage buckets: every prd-stage bucket on the prd Ceph cluster has an automatically refreshed copy on Google Drive. After the first successful nightly run, `iot-prd-attachments`, `electronics-inventory-prd-part-attachments` and the `design-assistant-prd` bucket are all in the mirror, and a bucket a prd release adds later through `terraform-modules/s3-storage` (HelmCharts `terraform-modules/s3-storage/main.tf:52-60`) is mirrored with nothing set per app.

"inventory what app-level backups already cover" — `decisions.md` §"Backup" carries a coverage list: each off-cluster mechanism, what it covers, how much history and which key, including the `postgres-pas` dumps through backup-server (scope `postgres-pas`, retention 90, HelmCharts `configs/prd/postgres-pas/_shared/infrastructure.tf:71-74`) and this mirror. It also has one line naming what is knowingly not covered (RBD volumes, CephFS, non-prd buckets), in place of "Offsite for production is a later item" (`decisions.md:593`).

"restore drill is part of acceptance (lesson from slice 005)." — after the first successful mirror run the operator has run the drill from the runbook in `/work/Ansible/docs/runbooks/`: `iot-prd-attachments` restored from Drive into a scratch bucket on dev Ceph, and `rclone check` against the live bucket, read with `backup-reader`'s read-only key, reports no differences. Closes only on the operator's output, never on a green gate.

"we should at least consider following the pattern set for Postgres." — the mirror follows the Postgres pattern for ownership. It is a production-gated job in the substrate's own chart (`storage`): off by default in the chart, on only in the prd cluster's values, its Terraform only under `configs/prd/`, as `postgres-backup` is (HelmCharts `charts/postgres-pas/values.yaml:100-101`, `configs/prd/postgres-pas/prd/values.yaml:53-54`, `configs/prd/postgres-pas/_shared/infrastructure.tf:71-74`). The dev cluster's storage release (`configs/dev/storage/`) deploys nothing new.

"It feels like it's unrealistic to want to do a daily snapshot of all S3 data keeping a history of 5 snapshots. Although, I do have 80 Gb available. Regardless I feel like this may need some smarts." — the mirror is incremental. A run over unchanged buckets uploads nothing and leaves no archive folder, and Drive holds the live data plus replaced or deleted objects only, never a full copy per run.

"A sync sounds perfect." — each prd-stage bucket is mirrored by an incremental, encrypted `rclone sync` to the existing Google Drive remote (`gdrive-pieter:Homelab Backups`, HelmCharts `configs/prd/storage/prd/values.yaml:15`), run from the `storage` chart. On Drive, file and folder names and contents are encrypted. Decrypted, the mirror holds `current/<bucket>/<object key path>` as live state and `archive/<bucket>/<run timestamp>/<object key path>` for what each run replaced or deleted (ruling W1).

One fleet-wide, read-only `backup-reader` RGW user, granted per bucket by a provider-attached bucket policy: `backup-reader` exists on prd with the admin capability `buckets=read` and nothing more, owns no bucket and cannot create one. It can list and read every prd-stage bucket, and every write or delete it attempts is refused.

The grant is on every prd-stage bucket on the prd cluster and nowhere else. The prd cluster's `design-assistant-dev`, `-tst` and `-uat` buckets carry no policy and are not mirrored. No `terraform-modules/s3-storage` call site sets anything for it. Releases on the dev cluster also run stage `prd` (HelmCharts `CLAUDE.md:45`) against a provider with no reader configured: the provider tests that `kc project test` runs (acceptance tests skip without `TF_ACC`, HomelabTerraformProvider `CLAUDE.md:45-47`) show that such a provider grants nothing and plans no change (ruling A1). The live proof, one manual dev deploy of an S3 release while srvk8sdev is up, is an outstanding operator action and not part of this criterion.

The new provider is inert for existing callers: a release that does not ask for the grant plans no change under it (every deploy floats to the newest provider, HelmCharts `tools/deploy/deploy_cli/tf.py:129-146`). When the grant lands, `iot-prd`, `electronics-inventory-prd` and `design-assistant-prd` update in place: no resource replaced, no bucket or object deleted (`terraform-modules/s3-storage/main.tf:57-59` keeps `prevent_destroy`).
A prd-stage bucket the mirror cannot list or read fails the run (the Job fails), never a skip; any rclone error fails the Job.
A bucket that disappears from RGW keeps its mirror copy untouched; the job never deletes a whole bucket's mirror.

After each successful sync the mirror keeps the 30 newest archive folders per bucket and prunes the rest. A run that moved nothing leaves no archive folder, so history is counted in changes, not days.

A critical Prometheus rule in the production Prometheus release, beside the other rules (HelmCharts `configs/prd/prometheus/prd/values.yaml:61`), on the mirror job's last successful run. Both edges of ruling D2 hold. One missed night stays quiet, however long the following run takes: the last-successful time is the Job's completion, not its schedule (live prd 2026-09-14: `storage-sync-cronjob` scheduled 00:10:00Z, last success 00:13:25Z), so the threshold carries a margin of a few hours, and every mirror run ends, succeeded or failed, within a bound inside that margin. Two consecutive missed nights fire, a few hours after the second failed run, and so does a mirror that has never succeeded. `postgres-backup` is not added to it.

The rclone crypt password and salt are in OpenBao `eso/prd/storage/prd/s3-mirror` and in Roboform next to the age key. The job reads them through the storage chart's ExternalSecret values (HelmCharts `configs/prd/storage/prd/values.yaml:43-59`) and never writes them to `rclone-backup-pvc`. `decisions.md`'s failure-domain inventory (`:108`) gains the key.

`decisions.md` §"Ceph RGW credentials" (`:86-95`, which today calls `csi-prd` the live posture at `:88`) reads in the present tense: per-app users are live and `csi-prd` is gone. `backup-reader` is its one recorded exception, with the reason.

The mirror uses the apps' endpoint `http://ceph:7480` (HelmCharts `_providers/clusters.yaml:22`), and `decisions.md`'s S3 endpoint convention (`:262`) states that endpoint instead of `https://ceph.home`.

The mirror runs on the existing `registry:5000/rclone-backup` image with its script shipped in the chart; no new image is built. A live probe on 2026-09-14 found Debian 13.6, rclone v1.75.1, curl 8.14.1 and python3 in the image.

`storage-sync-cronjob` and `storage-refresh-keys-cronjob` keep completing as before. The shared rclone config on `rclone-backup-pvc` gains no section, since both jobs treat every section there as a remote (DockerImages `rclone-backup/src/docker-entrypoint.sh:3`), and the mirror's schedule does not overlap theirs (HelmCharts `charts/storage/templates/storage-cronjobs.yaml:11-15`).

The runbook beside `openbao.md` covers restoring a bucket from the mirror (whole, or single objects and earlier versions from the archive), writing into the production bucket with the app's own key. It also covers reading the mirror with no cluster, from the Drive login and the Roboform-held crypt password and salt. It names where each credential it needs actually lives (ruling B2): the app's key pair in the Terraform-written Secret in the app's namespace (HelmCharts `terraform-modules/s3-storage/main.tf:62-72`), `backup-reader`'s key in the Terraform-written Secret in `storage-prd`, the crypt password and salt in OpenBao `eso/prd/storage/prd/s3-mirror` and Roboform, and the scratch user the drill creates on dev Ceph. Reading any of those values is the operator's keystroke or needs the operator's permission, and the drill reads the live bucket with `backup-reader`'s read-only key, never the app's.

The provider's reader user and bucket-grant behaviour carry unit tests in the `internal/s3storage` package's existing style, plus acceptance tests that skip without `TF_ACC`. The tests `kc project test` runs include the no-reader case V08 rests on: a resource asking for the grant on a provider with no reader configured grants nothing and plans no change.
